title: How Does a Trunk Get Wider?

scenes.visual: Title card 'How Does a Trunk Get Wider?' over a cross-section of an oak log. Reuses the first film's COLOUR MAP: dividing cells TEAL, elongating cells AMBER, mature cells GREEN; xylem and wood BROWN-GOLD, phloem VIOLET, cork DARK GREY. Cells are rounded rectangles, never molecular structures. Every number appears only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: The first film showed growth in length near the tips. So drive a nail into a tree trunk, a metre up. How high is it many years later?
scenes.caption: The first film showed growth in length near the tips. So drive a nail into a tree trunk, 1 m up. How high is it many years later?
scenes.visual: Brief replay: TEAL points glowing at the oak's tips. Then a hammer drives a nail into the trunk; a ruler beside it reads '1 m'. A clock spins to '20 years later?'.
scenes.narration: The first film showed growth in length near the tips. So drive a nail into a tree trunk, 1 m up. How high is it many years later?

scenes.visual: The trunk and nail hold still with a question mark beside the ruler.

scenes.tts: It is still at the same height. That part of the trunk stopped lengthening long ago. A tree gets taller only in young shoots near its tips. But the trunk keeps getting wider.
scenes.visual: Years pass: the crown rises well above as the young shoots at the top lengthen, the nail stays at the '1 m' mark, and the trunk around it thickens outward on both sides (schematic).
scenes.narration: It is still at the same height. That part of the trunk stopped lengthening long ago. A tree gets taller only in young shoots near its tips. But the trunk keeps getting wider.

scenes.tts: Width comes from a thin cylinder of dividing cells inside the stem, the vascular cambium. It lies between the xylem and the phloem. It is a lateral meristem, running along older stems and roots.
scenes.visual: The trunk turns translucent, revealing a thin TEAL cylinder just under the bark, running through the older trunk, branches and woody roots and fading out before the young shoot and root tips, labelled 'vascular cambium (lateral meristem)'.
scenes.narration: Width comes from a thin cylinder of dividing cells inside the stem, the vascular cambium. It lies between the xylem and the phloem. It is a lateral meristem, running along older stems and roots.

scenes.tts: Cut a thin strip from the centre of the trunk out to its surface. The vascular cambium is one thin teal line inside it.
scenes.visual: A narrow radial strip lifts out of the trunk and lies flat across the screen, 'centre' at left, 'surface' at right. A single TEAL line of cells sits near the right end.
scenes.narration: Cut a thin strip from the centre of the trunk out to its surface. The vascular cambium is one thin teal line inside it.

scenes.tts: When a cambium cell divides, some daughters are pushed inward. They become secondary xylem, which is wood.
scenes.visual: One TEAL cell divides; a daughter slides left and turns BROWN-GOLD, joining a growing BROWN-GOLD block labelled 'secondary xylem = wood'.
scenes.narration: When a cambium cell divides, some daughters are pushed inward. They become secondary xylem, which is wood.

scenes.tts: Other daughters are pushed outward. They become secondary phloem, the tissue that carries sugars from the leaves to the rest of the plant.
scenes.visual: Another division; a daughter slides right and turns VIOLET, joining a thin VIOLET band labelled 'secondary phloem'. Tiny sugar dots drift along it.
scenes.narration: Other daughters are pushed outward. They become secondary phloem, the tissue that carries sugars from the leaves to the rest of the plant.

scenes.tts: In a temperate oak, the cambium works in spring and summer and rests in winter. Spring wood has large vessels. Late summer wood has smaller ones.
scenes.visual: A season dial turns. Spring: BROWN-GOLD wood with conspicuously large vessels added, labelled 'earlywood: large vessels'. Late summer: denser BROWN-GOLD wood with smaller vessels, labelled 'latewood: smaller vessels'. Winter: the TEAL line pauses, dimmed.
scenes.narration: In a temperate oak, the cambium works in spring and summer and rests in winter. Spring wood has large vessels. Late summer wood has smaller ones.

scenes.tts: Where one summer's dense wood meets the next spring's large vessels, a line appears. Each year usually leaves one ring.
scenes.visual: The dial turns again; a sharp boundary appears between dense latewood and the next band of large spring vessels, labelled 'annual ring'. Several years repeat, building a row of rings across the strip, labelled 'usually one per year'.
scenes.narration: Where one summer's dense wood meets the next spring's large vessels, a line appears. Each year usually leaves one ring.

scenes.tts: As the trunk widens, its old skin, the epidermis, splits. A second lateral meristem, the cork cambium, usually forms just beneath it. Outward it makes cork, whose cells have waterproofed walls. Inward it makes a thin living layer, the phelloderm. Cork, cork cambium and phelloderm together form the periderm. The periderm replaces the epidermis.
scenes.visual: At the strip's right edge, the thin outer skin (epidermis) cracks and flakes away. Just beneath it a second thin line appears, labelled 'cork cambium', making DARK GREY cork cells outward ('cork: waterproofed walls') and a thin living layer inward ('phelloderm'). A bracket over all three reads 'periderm: replaces the epidermis'. Hold this frame a beat longer than the others.
scenes.narration: As the trunk widens, its old skin, the epidermis, splits. A second lateral meristem, the cork cambium, usually forms just beneath it. Outward it makes cork, whose cells have waterproofed walls. Inward it makes a thin living layer, the phelloderm. Cork, cork cambium and phelloderm together form the periderm. The periderm replaces the epidermis.

scenes.tts: Bark is everything outside the vascular cambium. So its inner part is living phloem, not only dead cork.
scenes.visual: A bracket sweeps from the TEAL vascular cambium out to the surface, labelled 'bark'. Inside the bracket the VIOLET phloem glows 'living'; the DARK GREY cork is labelled 'dead'.
scenes.narration: Bark is everything outside the vascular cambium. So its inner part is living phloem, not only dead cork.

scenes.tts: This is the first film's rule, turned sideways. Over one year, count the new wood cells in a row out from the cambium. Multiply by their average width. Cell widths change through the season, so the average matters. That gives the width of the ring.
scenes.visual: The rule from the first film reappears with its TEAL and AMBER underlines, then rotates ninety degrees to lie across the strip, along one radial row of wood cells: 'one year: ring width = new wood cells in one radial row x their average width'. The spring and late-summer cells in that row, of different widths, are tinted to show they are averaged.
scenes.narration: This is the first film's rule, turned sideways. Over one year, count the new wood cells in a row out from the cambium. Multiply by their average width. Cell widths change through the season, so the average matters. That gives the width of the ring.

scenes.tts: Maize has no conventional vascular cambium. Its bundles are scattered, and it makes no wood. It grew tall from its shoot tip and from meristems at the bases of its leaves and internodes.
scenes.visual: A maize stalk cross-section: scattered small bundles, each with a BROWN-GOLD and a VIOLET patch, and no TEAL cylinder, no rings; label 'no conventional vascular cambium: no wood'. Then a side view with TEAL glows at the shoot tip and at the bases of leaves and internodes.
scenes.narration: Maize has no conventional vascular cambium. Its bundles are scattered, and it makes no wood. It grew tall from its shoot tip and from meristems at the bases of its leaves and internodes.

scenes.tts: So a tree's shoot tips add height. Its vascular cambium adds width and wood.
scenes.visual: Split screen: the oak's young shoots glowing TEAL with an up arrow 'height'; the trunk's TEAL cambium cylinder with outward arrows 'wider: wood inward, phloem outward'.
scenes.narration: So a tree's shoot tips add height. Its vascular cambium adds width and wood.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex. LINE: 'The vascular cambium widens a trunk: wood inward, phloem outward.'
